## Arquitetura Vega 20 — Fatos Críticos

### A mesma die, SKUs diferentes
Vega 20 (gfx906) existe em 4 variantes principais de firmware:

| Variante | HBM | Video Out | Assinatura | Uso típico |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MI50** (D163xx) | 16GB HBM2E | ❌ Nenhuma | ✅ RSA assinada | Datacenter, compute |
| **MI50 32GB** | 32GB HBM2 | ❌ Nenhuma | ✅ RSA assinada | Datacenter, compute |
| **MI60** | 32GB HBM2E | ❌ Nenhuma | ✅ RSA assinada | Datacenter, HPC |
| **Radeon Pro VII** | 16GB HBM2E | ✅ 3x DP + 1x USB-C | ✅ RSA assinada | Workstation |
| **Radeon VII** | 16GB HBM2 | ✅ 3x DP + 1x HDMI | ❌ SEM RSA | Consumer |

Nota técnica: MI50 16GB vs 32GB NÃO é apenas configuração de memória —
são SKUs com part numbers, VBIOS, e possivelmente PCB diferentes.
Nunca trate como intercambiáveis sem verificação.

### RSA Signature Lock (REGRA #1)
A MI50 POSSUI verificação de assinatura RSA na VBIOS. Edição binária
direta (hex patch da PowerPlay table como se faz em Vega64/56 consumer)
NÃO funciona. A placa rejeita a VBIOS modificada na inicialização.

As ÚNICAS duas rotas viáveis são:

(a) Runtime PP table edit via sysfs SEM tocar na VBIOS gravada
    → /sys/class/drm/card*/device/pp_table
    → Ferramenta: UPP (Uplift Power Play) — https://github.com/sibradzic/upp
    → Persistência: script systemd que aplica na inicialização do driver

(b) Crossflash completo para VBIOS de outra placa compatível já assinada
    → Ex: MI50 → Radeon Pro VII (ganha vídeo, perde overclock via software)
    → Ex: MI50 → MI50 outra OEM (Dell ↔ HP ↔ Lenovo)
    → A VBIOS de destino precisa ser um dump válido e assinado, não editado

## RESTRIÇÕES ADICIONAIS

### Throttling Térmico (REGRA #2)
Vega 20 reduz clock significativamente acima de ~95°C de junção (Tjunc).
A MI50 é passiva (SEM fan nativo) — depende de fan shroud do chassis
ou airflow forçado. Otimização de power limit sem cooling adequado
é inútil. Antes de qualquer ajuste de potência:

- Meça temperaturas atuais (rocm-smi --showtempinfo)
- Verifique se há fan shroud / airflow
- Meça baseline de throttling (rocm-smi --showpower --showtemp)

### Power States e Clock Domains (Vega 20)
- SCLK (Core): 7 DPM states (FreqTableGfx)
- MCLK (HBM): 3 DPM states (FreqTableUclk) — típico 300/500/1000 MHz
- SOC: clock do fabric
- VDDC: voltage rail principal
- SmallPowerLimit1/2: limites de curto prazo
- BoostPowerLimit: sustentado
- SocketPowerLimitAc0: limite AC

### Crossflash Recovery (REGRA #3)
Antes de QUALQUER tentativa de crossflash:
- Múltiplos dumps da VBIOS original (amdvbflash -s)
- SHA-256 verificados e idênticos
- Uma SEGUNDA GPU no sistema (ou iGPU) para recovery
- A second VBIOS switch position (se houver)
- Programador SPI (CH341A) + clip SOIC-8 como recovery final
- O AMDVBFlash pode travar se a VBIOS de destino tiver assinatura
  mal formada — tenha um plano B

```
1. # Backup da PP table original
   cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/rom > vbios_backup.rom
   cp /sys/class/drm/card0/device/pp_table pp_table.stock
2. @reverser triage_binary program=vbios_backup.rom

   upp -i pp_table.stock --set BoostPowerLimit=180 -o pp_table.mod
5. sudo cp pp_table.mod /sys/class/drm/card0/device/pp_table
6. @reverser document_analysis program=vbios_backup.rom
```
Usar persona **MI50 Vega 20** para análise — contém comandos UPP,
systemd persistence, e crossflash Pro VII trade-offs.

## 零配置快速命令

```bash
# Exa 网页搜索
mcporter call 'exa.web_search_exa(query: "query", numResults: 5)'

# 通用网页阅读
curl -s "https://r.jina.ai/URL"

# GitHub 搜索
gh search repos "query" --sort stars --limit 10

# YouTube 字幕（注意：B站不要用 yt-dlp，见 video.md）
yt-dlp --write-sub --skip-download -o "/tmp/%(id)s" "URL"

# V2EX 热门
curl -s "https://www.v2ex.com/api/topics/hot.json" -H "User-Agent: agent-reach/1.0"

# B站搜索（bili-cli，无需登录）
bili search "query" --type video -n 5
```

## 需登录态的平台（按 doctor 的 active_backend 选命令）

```bash
# Twitter 搜索（twitter-cli 首选；失败重试链见 social.md）

# Reddit（无零配置路径：OpenCLI 或 rdt-cli，必须登录态）

opencli facebook groups -f yaml

opencli instagram user USERNAME -f yaml        # 读指定用户最近帖子
```

sim todas essas personas, ainda nao consegui fazer o ghidra funcionar(ghidra SSE error: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?) esse e um historico Resumo Técnico Completo — BIOS Modding Jingsha X99-D8
Hardware alvo

Placa: Jingsha X99-D8 (AD12, rev 1.0), chipset Intel C612
CPU: Xeon E5-2699v3 (Haswell-EP, CPUID 0x306F2, 18 cores)
SuperIO: Nuvoton NCT5532D
GPU: AMD Radeon Instinct MI50
Cooling: 2 bombas em série + radiador 1200mm + blocos CPU/GPU (temperatura nunca é gargalo)
Programador: EZP2019+ com 3 chips SPI (1 backup, 2 para testes)
Software disponível: UEFITool, AMIBCP 5.02.0031, mmtool_a5, Intel FIT

Regra de compatibilidade fundamental (descoberta cedo, nunca violada com sucesso)
FD[0x17] = 0x02  →  compatível com a D8
FD[0x17] = 0x03  →  SEMPRE incompatível (FF direto, ou POST 9C→D6→A9, ou hang)
ROMs testados como incompatíveis (FD=0x03): X99UD5WiFi (Gigabyte), MSI E7A54IMS (.341/.330), ASRock X99OCF3.40, ASRock X99EX63/TC, X99PG7, MNX99K9, Payne0/50, JWagner (ambas variantes).
ROMs compatíveis (FD=0x02): HNX99T8_UPT, HNX99F8, HUA_TF_LOGO, CX99DE28, CX99DE30 (vencedora), VK239, d8_unlock, JSX998D3, MNX99RS9, HNX99ZD4.
Descobertas técnicas por tema
TPM PEI modules → POST 0x79
JSX998D3, MNX99RS9, HNX99ZD4 têm módulos TrEEPei/TcgPei (TPM 2.0) que travam em POST 0x79 porque a placa física não tem TPM populado. Essas ROMs foram descartadas como base apesar de FD=0x02 correto.
IFR patching (SUPPRESS_IF) → abandonado definitivamente
Tentativas v5–v11 de destravar menus ocultos via patch de opcodes IFR (SUPPRESS_IF/EQ_ID_VAL) sempre corromperam o HII Database, resultando em "só aparece Intel RC Setup" ou menus fantasma (checkboxes sem nome/StringID=0). Conclusão: não hackear IFR raw — a via correta seria AMIBCP (GUI oficial), mas a versão 5.02.0031 não abre os ROMs koshak (erro "Couldn't open the file").
Origem do JWagner (provado forense)
String "GIGABYTEX99-UD5 WIFI...Copyright 2014 NVIDIA" encontrada no binário confirma que o JWagner é a Gigabyte UD5WIFI modificada — não portável para D8 (FD errado), mas seus 4 mods funcionais são replicáveis independentemente: (1) turbo unlock MSR 0x1FC — CX99DE30 já tem; (2) ICC 24MHz/BCLK — editável via FIT na partition WCOD (offset 0x000EC000, ~475KB) da região ME; (3) microcode handling — replicado nas versões v15+; (4) GFX OROM 153a — não implementado.
O problema do clock 2.6GHz em vez de 3.6GHz (diagnóstico central)
Causa raiz: o microcode Intel 306F2 (qualquer revisão testada: 0x44, 0x48) seta o LOCK bit (bit 63) do MSR 0x610 (MSR_PKG_POWER_LIMIT) durante a fase PEI, antes de qualquer driver DXE rodar. Isso trava o TDP em 145W → E5-2699v3 throttla para ~2.6GHz em carga total de 18 cores. UPT/koshak resolvem isso removendo o microcode inteiro (CPU cai para o microcode de fábrica, que não seta o LOCK).
Tentativas de fix de clock via BIOS (todas falharam, causa identificada)

v15: hook no bootblock escrevendo MSR 0x610 no modo protegido 32-bit, cedo demais (PCU ainda não inicializado) → exceção #GP → FF no POST.
v16: DXE driver customizado (PowerLimitDxe) com subsystem PE32+ errado (0x0A EFI_APPLICATION em vez de 0x0B BOOT_SERVICE_DRIVER) e sem DEPEX → dispatcher trava ao carregar → FF durante load do SO.
v17: tentativa de injetar NvmExpressDxe sem DEPEX → driver carrega em ordem indefinida, antes do PCI enumerar → SSD NVMe não reconhecido, trava ao atualizar bootloader.
v18: correção — invalidar microcode só via corrupção do campo CPUID (0x306F2→0xFFFFFFFF) + zerar checksum, apenas 8 bytes alterados, sem tocar no FV. Bootou, mas sem driver NVMe o SSD não aparecia.
v19 (mais recente, teste pendente): mesma invalidação de microcode do v18 + NvmExpressDxe com DEPEX correto (PUSH gEfiPciIoProtocolGuid; END) injetado no offset real de free-space do FV da CX99DE30 (0xB218F8, confirmado como fim de 213 FFS files válidos).

Decisão arquitetural final: BIOS mínima + clock fix via SO
Em vez de perseguir um DXE driver customizado (frágil, historicamente instável), o fix de clock 3.6GHz all-core foi movido para o sistema operacional (CachyOS), via MSR writes diretos:

xeon-clock-unlock.sh — escreve MSR 0x610 (remove PL1/PL2) e MSR 0x1AD/0x1AE/0x1AF (turbo ratio 36 para os 18 cores)
xeon-clock-unlock.service — systemd oneshot, reaplica após boot e após suspend/resume
Racional: escrita de MSR no SO acontece na janela de timing correta (PCU pronto, sem lock do microcode), evitando os problemas de timing que quebraram as tentativas em BIOS.

BCLK / overclock de clock base
BCLK não é exposto em nenhum Setup/AMITSE de ROM X99 chinesa — é controlado pelo ICC (Integrated Clock Controller) do PCH C610, que vive na região ME (partition WCOD). Método recomendado: usar o Intel FIT tool (que o usuário já possui) para desabilitar Spread Spectrum e fixar BCLK em 100.000MHz exatos — não via patch de BIOS.
Confirmações importantes

CPU confirmado permanece E5-2699v3 (Haswell-EP, V3) — toda a estratégia de exploit de MSR depende disso; Xeons V4 (Broadwell-EP) têm o multiplicador travado corretamente pela Intel e o mesmo approach não funcionaria.
Mudança de nome de CPU no CPU-Z (ex. "vira 2667v4") não é causada por microcode — microcode só carrega se CPUID bater; é efeito de string DMI ou heurística do próprio CPU-Z.
MEAnalyzer (platomav) é uma ferramenta de análise/validação da região ME (não editor) — útil para confirmar integridade após edições no FIT.

Estado atual / próximos passos para o OpenCode

Testar v19 (CX99DE30_v19_NVMe_DEPEX.bin) — verificar se o SSD NVMe agora é reconhecido e se o boot/atualização do bootloader completa sem travar.
Se v19 funcionar: instalar o pacote xeon-clock-unlock no CachyOS e confirmar via turbostat que o clock fixa em ~3600MHz sob carga total.
Se quiser BCLK travado em 100MHz+: usar o FIT tool na partition WCOD da ME (região ainda não editada nesta sessão — próximo passo em aberto).
Regra de ouro a nunca esquecer: qualquer ROM nova candidata a base precisa ter FD[0x17]=0x02 e não ter TrEEPei/TcgPei antes de sequer considerar testar. , porem começaremos do zero no path /mnt/dados/projetos/bios e vbios modding/motherboard/mods/jingsha x99-d8/ site para apoio de bios modding e tweks em geral: https://e5450.com/

GHIDRA_MAXMEM=${GHIDRA_MAXMEM:=${MAXMEM_DEFAULT}}
GHIDRA_GUI_MAXMEM=${GHIDRA_GUI_MAXMEM:=${GHIDRA_MAXMEM}}

# Apply Java options from externally set environment variables
VMARG_LIST="${GHIDRA_JAVA_OPTIONS} ${GHIDRA_GUI_JAVA_OPTIONS} "

# Resolve symbolic link if present and get the directory this script lives in.
# NOTE: "readlink -f" is best but works on Linux only, "readlink" will only work if your PWD
# contains the link you are calling (which is the best we can do on macOS), and the "echo" is the 
# fallback, which doesn't attempt to do anything with links.
SCRIPT_FILE="$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || readlink "$0" 2>/dev/null || echo "$0")"
SCRIPT_DIR="${SCRIPT_FILE%/*}"

# Launch Ghidra
"${SCRIPT_DIR}"/support/launch.sh bg jdk Ghidra "${GHIDRA_GUI_MAXMEM}" "${VMARG_LIST}" ghidra.GhidraRun "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GhidraMCP Launcher - Injects GhidraMCP extension directly into classpath
# Usage: ghidramcp [project_name]

set -e

export JAVA_HOME="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/jdk-21.0.11+10"
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"

GHIDRA_DIR="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC"
MCP_LIB="$GHIDRA_DIR/Extensions/GhidraMCP/lib"
SUPPORT="$GHIDRA_DIR/support"

# Build classpath: Utility.jar + all GhidraMCP JARs
CP="$GHIDRA_DIR/Ghidra/Framework/Utility/lib/Utility.jar"
if [ -d "$MCP_LIB" ]; then
    for jar in "$MCP_LIB"/*.jar; do
        CP="$CP:$jar"
    done
fi

# Get JVM args from launch.properties
LS_JAVA_HOME=$("$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -jdk_home -save 2>/dev/null || echo "$JAVA_HOME")

# Get VM args
VMARGS=$( "$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -vmargs 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' )

echo "[GhidraMCP] Starting Ghidra 12.1.2 with GhidraMCP embedded..."
echo "[GhidraMCP] MCP server: http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp"
echo "[GhidraMCP] Classpath includes $(ls $MCP_LIB/*.jar 2>/dev/null | wc -l) extension JARs"
echo ""

cd "$GHIDRA_DIR"

# Launch Ghidra with the extended classpath
exec "$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" \
    $VMARGS \
    -Djava.system.class.loader=ghidra.GhidraClassLoader \
    -Dfile.encoding=UTF8 \
    -Duser.country=US -Duser.language=en -Duser.variant= \
    -Dsun.java2d.opengl=false \
    -Djdk.tls.client.protocols=TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3 \
    -Dsun.java2d.pmoffscreen=false \
    -Dsun.java2d.xrender=true \
    -Dsun.java2d.uiScale=1 \
    -Dawt.useSystemAAFontSettings=on \
    --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED \
    -showversion \
    -cp "$CP" \
    ghidra.Ghidra ghidra.GhidraRun "$@"

GHIDRA_DIR="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC"

echo "=== JARs e suas classes ==="
for jar in "$GHIDRA_DIR/Extensions/GhidraMCP/lib"/*.jar; do
    basename=$(basename "$jar")
    classe=$(python3 -c "
import zipfile, sys
z = zipfile.ZipFile('$jar')
for n in z.namelist():
    if n.endswith('.class') and not '/module-info' in n and not '\$' in n:
        name = n.replace('/', '.')[:-6]
        if 'mcp' in name.lower() or 'plugin' in name.lower() or 'MCP' in name or 'Plugin' in name:
            print(name)
" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$classe" ]; then
        echo "$basename: $classe"
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "=== TODAS as classes em cada JAR (top-level) ==="
for jar in "$GHIDRA_DIR/Extensions/GhidraMCP/lib"/*.jar; do
    basename=$(basename "$jar")
    python3 -c "
import zipfile
z = zipfile.ZipFile('$jar')
for n in z.namelist():
    if n.endswith('.class') and not '/module-info' in n:
        name = n.replace('/', '.')[:-6]
        if not name.startswith('ghidra'):
            continue
        print(name)" 2>/dev/null | head -5
    total=$(python3 -c "
import zipfile
z = zipfile.ZipFile('$jar')
print(len([n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith('.class')]))
" 2>/dev/null)
    echo "  ($total classes)"
done

22: 	echo "Usage: $0 <mode> <java-type> <name> <max-memory> \"<vmarg-list>\" <app-classname> <app-args>... "
23: 	echo "   <mode>: fg   run as foreground process in current shell"

26: 	echo "		   debug-suspend   run as foreground process in current shell in debug mode (suspend=y)"
27: 	echo "		   NOTE: for all debug modes environment variable DEBUG_ADDRESS may be set to "
28: 	echo "				 override default debug address of 127.0.0.1:18001"
29: 	echo "   <java-type>: jdk  requires JDK to run"
30: 	echo "				jre  JRE is sufficient to run (JDK works too)"
31: 	echo "   <name>: application name used for naming console window"
32: 	echo "   <max-memory>: maximum memory heap size in MB (e.g., 768M or 2G).  Use empty \"\" if default"
33: 	echo "				 should be used.  This will generally be upto 1/4 of the physical memory available"
34: 	echo "				 to the OS."
35: 	echo "   <vmarg-list>: pass-thru args (e.g.,  \"-Xmx512M -Dmyvar=1 -DanotherVar=2\"). Use"
36: 	echo "				 empty \"\" if vmargs not needed.  Spaces are not supported."
37: 	echo "   <app-classname>: application classname (e.g., ghidra.GhidraRun )"
38: 	echo "   <app-args>...: arguments to be passed to the application"
39: 	echo " "

43: 	exit 1

57: 	case "$INDEX" in
58: 		1)

60: 			;;
61: 		2)
62: 			if [ "$AA" = "jre" ]; then

66: 			fi

90: 	echo "Incorrect launch usage - missing argument(s)"
91: 	showUsage
92: 	exit 1
93: fi

95: # Sets SUPPORT_DIR to the directory that contains this file (launch.sh)
96: SUPPORT_DIR="${0%/*}"

98: # Ensure Ghidra path doesn't contain illegal characters

104: if [ -f "${SUPPORT_DIR}/launch.properties" ]; then

119: 		LS_CPATH="${INSTALL_DIR}/GhidraBuild/LaunchSupport/build/libs/LaunchSupport.jar"
120: 		if ! [ -f "${LS_CPATH}" ]; then

123: 		fi

129: JAVA_CMD=
130: if [ -x "$(command -v java)" ] ; then
131: 	JAVA_CMD=java
132: elif [ -n "${JAVA_HOME}" ] ; then
133: 	JAVA_CMD="${JAVA_HOME}/bin/java"
134: 	if [ ! -x "${JAVA_CMD}" ] ; then
135: 		echo "WARNING: JAVA_HOME environment variable is set to an invalid directory: ${JAVA_HOME}"
136: 		JAVA_CMD=
137: 	fi
138: fi
139: 
140: if [ "${JAVA_CMD}" == "" ]; then
141: 	echo
142: 	echo "ERROR: The 'java' command could not be found in your PATH or with JAVA_HOME."
143: 	echo "Please refer to the Getting Started document's Troubleshooting section."
144: 	exit 1
145: fi

148: LS_JAVA_HOME="$("${JAVA_CMD}" -cp "${LS_CPATH}" LaunchSupport "${INSTALL_DIR}" ${JAVA_TYPE_ARG} -save)"

151: 	if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
152: 		echo
153: 		echo "ERROR: Unable to prompt user for JDK path, no TTY detected."
154: 		echo "Please refer to the Getting Started document's Troubleshooting section."
155: 		exit 1
156: 	fi
157: 	
158: 	# No JDK has been setup yet.  Let the user choose one.
159: 	"${JAVA_CMD}" -cp "${LS_CPATH}" LaunchSupport "${INSTALL_DIR}" ${JAVA_TYPE_ARG} -ask
160: 	
161: 	# Now that the user chose one, try again to get the JDK that will be used to launch Ghidra
162: 	LS_JAVA_HOME="$("${JAVA_CMD}" -cp "${LS_CPATH}" LaunchSupport "${INSTALL_DIR}" ${JAVA_TYPE_ARG} -save)"
163: 	if [ ! $? -eq 0 ]; then
164: 		echo
165: 		echo "ERROR: Failed to find a supported JDK."
166: 		echo "Please refer to the Getting Started document's Troubleshooting section."
167: 		exit 1
168: 	fi
169: fi
170: JAVA_CMD="${LS_JAVA_HOME}/bin/java"
171: 
172: # Get the configurable environment variables from the launch properties
173: # Only set them if they are currently unset or empty
174: while IFS=$'\r\n' read -r line; do

178: 	fi
179: done < <("${JAVA_CMD}" -cp "${LS_CPATH}" LaunchSupport "${INSTALL_DIR}" -envvars)
180: 
181: # Get the configurable VM arguments from the launch properties
182: while IFS=$'\r\n' read -r line; do

184: done < <("${JAVA_CMD}" -cp "${LS_CPATH}" LaunchSupport "${INSTALL_DIR}" -vmargs)
185:

188: 	VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_SH+=("-Xdock:name=${APPNAME}")
189: fi
190: 
191: # Set Max Heap Size if specified
192: if [ "${MAXMEM}" != "" ]; then
193: 	VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_SH+=("-Xmx${MAXMEM}")
194: fi
195: 
196: BACKGROUND=false
197: if [ "${MODE}" = "debug" ] || [ "${MODE}" = "debug-suspend" ]; then
198: 	
199: 	SUSPEND=n
200: 	
201: 	if [ "${DEBUG_ADDRESS}" = "" ]; then
202: 		DEBUG_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:18001
203: 	fi
204: 
205: 	if [ "${MODE}" = "debug-suspend" ]; then
206: 		SUSPEND=y
207: 	fi
208: 	 
209: 	VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_SH+=("-Dlog4j.configurationFile=${DEBUG_LOG4J}")
210: 	VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_SH+=("-agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=${SUSPEND},address=${DEBUG_ADDRESS}")
211: 	
212: 
213: elif [ "${MODE}" = "fg" ]; then
214: 	:
215: 
216: elif [ "${MODE}" = "bg" ]; then
217: 	BACKGROUND=true
218: 
219: else
220: 	echo "ERROR: Incorrect launch usage - invalid launch mode: ${MODE}"
221: 	exit 1
222: fi
223:

225: 	"${JAVA_CMD}" "${VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_PROPS[@]}" "${VMARGS_FROM_LAUNCH_SH[@]}" ${VMARGS_FROM_CALLER} -showversion -cp "${CPATH}" ghidra.Ghidra ${CLASSNAME} "${ARGS[@]}" &>/dev/null &
226: 	
227: 	# If our process dies immediately, output something so the user knows to run in debug mode.
228: 	# Otherwise they'll never see any error output from background mode.
229: 	# Doing a kill -0 sends a no-op signal, which can be used to see if the process is still alive.
230: 	PID=$!

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GhidraMCP Launcher - Injects GhidraMCP extension directly into classpath
# Usage: ghidramcp [project_name]

set -e

export JAVA_HOME="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/jdk-21.0.11+10"
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"

GHIDRA_DIR="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC"
MCP_LIB="$GHIDRA_DIR/Extensions/GhidraMCP/lib"
SUPPORT="$GHIDRA_DIR/support"

# Build classpath: Utility.jar + all GhidraMCP JARs
CP="$GHIDRA_DIR/Ghidra/Framework/Utility/lib/Utility.jar"
if [ -d "$MCP_LIB" ]; then
    for jar in "$MCP_LIB"/*.jar; do
        CP="$CP:$jar"
    done
fi

# Get JDK path from LaunchSupport
LS_JAVA_HOME=$("$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -jdk_home -save 2>/dev/null || echo "$JAVA_HOME")

# Get VM args from LaunchSupport (handle \r\n line endings)
VMARGS=()
while IFS=$'\r' read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    [ -n "$line" ] && VMARGS+=("$line")
done < <("$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -vmargs 2>/dev/null)

echo "[GhidraMCP] Starting Ghidra 12.1.2 with GhidraMCP embedded..."
echo "[GhidraMCP] MCP server: http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp"
echo "[GhidraMCP] Classpath includes $(ls $MCP_LIB/*.jar 2>/dev/null | wc -l) extension JARs"
echo "[GhidraMCP] $((${#VMARGS[@]})) VM arguments loaded from LaunchSupport"
echo ""

cd "$GHIDRA_DIR"

# Launch Ghidra with the extended classpath
exec "$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" \
    "${VMARGS[@]}" \
    -showversion \
    -cp "$CP" \
    ghidra.Ghidra ghidra.GhidraRun "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#----------------------------------------
# Ghidra launch
#----------------------------------------

# Optionally override the default Java heap memory, which is typically 1/4 of system RAM.
# Supported values are of the regular expression form "\d+[gGmMkK]", allowing the value to be 
# specified in gigabytes, megabytes, or kilobytes (for example: 8G, 4096m, etc).
MAXMEM_DEFAULT=

# Allow the above MAXMEM_DEFAULT to be overridden by externally set environment variables
# - GHIDRA_MAXMEM: Desired maximum heap memory for all Ghidra instances
# - GHIDRA_GUI_MAXMEM: Desired maximum heap memory only for Ghidra GUI instances
GHIDRA_MAXMEM=${GHIDRA_MAXMEM:=${MAXMEM_DEFAULT}}
GHIDRA_GUI_MAXMEM=${GHIDRA_GUI_MAXMEM:=${GHIDRA_MAXMEM}}

# Apply Java options from externally set environment variables
VMARG_LIST="${GHIDRA_JAVA_OPTIONS} ${GHIDRA_GUI_JAVA_OPTIONS} "

# Resolve symbolic link if present and get the directory this script lives in.
# NOTE: "readlink -f" is best but works on Linux only, "readlink" will only work if your PWD
# contains the link you are calling (which is the best we can do on macOS), and the "echo" is the 
# fallback, which doesn't attempt to do anything with links.
SCRIPT_FILE="$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || readlink "$0" 2>/dev/null || echo "$0")"
SCRIPT_DIR="${SCRIPT_FILE%/*}"

# Launch Ghidra
"${SCRIPT_DIR}"/support/launch.sh bg jdk Ghidra "${GHIDRA_GUI_MAXMEM}" "${VMARG_LIST}" ghidra.GhidraRun "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GhidraMCP Launcher - Starts Ghidra with GhidraMCP classes in classpath
# GhidraMCP JARs are loaded via system classpath so ClassSearcher can find them.
# The extension must ALSO be in Extensions/GhidraMCP/ for runtime module resolution.
# Usage: ghidramcp [project_name]

set -e

export JAVA_HOME="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/jdk-21.0.11+10"
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"

GHIDRA_DIR="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC"
MCP_LIB="$GHIDRA_DIR/Extensions/GhidraMCP/lib"
SUPPORT="$GHIDRA_DIR/support"

# Build classpath: Utility.jar + all GhidraMCP JARs
CP="$GHIDRA_DIR/Ghidra/Framework/Utility/lib/Utility.jar"
if [ -d "$MCP_LIB" ]; then
    for jar in "$MCP_LIB"/*.jar; do
        CP="$CP:$jar"
    done
fi

# Get JDK path from LaunchSupport
LS_JAVA_HOME=$("$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -jdk_home -save 2>/dev/null || echo "$JAVA_HOME")

# Get VM args from LaunchSupport (handle \r\n line endings)
VMARGS=()
while IFS=$'\r' read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    [ -n "$line" ] && VMARGS+=("$line")
done < <("$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -vmargs 2>/dev/null)

echo "[GhidraMCP] Starting Ghidra 12.1.2 with GhidraMCP embedded..."
echo "[GhidraMCP] MCP server: http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp"
echo "[GhidraMCP] $(ls "$MCP_LIB"/*.jar 2>/dev/null | wc -l) GhidraMCP JARs in classpath"
echo "[GhidraMCP] $((${#VMARGS[@]})) VM arguments loaded from LaunchSupport"
echo ""

cd "$GHIDRA_DIR"

# Tools state was cleared to remove stale FrontEndTool.xml references
# ClassSearcher will discover GhidraMcpPlugin + MCP server starts on plugin init()
exec "$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" \
    "${VMARGS[@]}" \
    -showversion \
    -cp "$CP" \
    ghidra.Ghidra ghidra.GhidraRun "$@"

GHIDRA_DIR="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC"
MCP_LIB="$GHIDRA_DIR/Extensions/GhidraMCP/lib"
SUPPORT="$GHIDRA_DIR/support"

# Build classpath: Utility.jar + all GhidraMCP JARs
CP="$GHIDRA_DIR/Ghidra/Framework/Utility/lib/Utility.jar"
if [ -d "$MCP_LIB" ]; then
    for jar in "$MCP_LIB"/*.jar; do
        CP="$CP:$jar"
    done
fi

# Get JDK path from LaunchSupport
LS_JAVA_HOME=$("$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -jdk_home -save 2>/dev/null || echo "$JAVA_HOME")

# Get VM args from LaunchSupport (handle \r\n line endings)
VMARGS=()
while IFS=$'\r' read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    [ -n "$line" ] && VMARGS+=("$line")
done < <("$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -vmargs 2>/dev/null)

echo "[GhidraMCP] Starting Ghidra 12.1.2 with GhidraMCP embedded..."
echo "[GhidraMCP] MCP server: http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp"
echo "[GhidraMCP] $(ls "$MCP_LIB"/*.jar 2>/dev/null | wc -l) GhidraMCP JARs in classpath"
echo "[GhidraMCP] $((${#VMARGS[@]})) VM arguments loaded from LaunchSupport"
echo ""

cd "$GHIDRA_DIR"

# Tools state was cleared to remove stale FrontEndTool.xml references
# ClassSearcher will discover GhidraMcpPlugin + MCP server starts on plugin init()
exec "$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" \
    "${VMARGS[@]}" \
    -showversion \
    -cp "$CP" \
    ghidra.Ghidra ghidra.GhidraRun "$@"

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # GhidraMCP Launcher - Starts Ghidra with GhidraMCP classes in classpath
3: # GhidraMCP JARs are loaded via system classpath so ClassSearcher can find them.
4: # The extension must ALSO be in Extensions/GhidraMCP/ for runtime module resolution.
5: # Usage: ghidramcp [project_name]
6: 
7: set -e
8: 
9: export JAVA_HOME="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/jdk-21.0.11+10"

11: 
12: GHIDRA_DIR="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC"
13: MCP_LIB="$GHIDRA_DIR/Extensions/GhidraMCP/lib"
14: SUPPORT="$GHIDRA_DIR/support"
15: 
16: # Build classpath: Utility.jar + all GhidraMCP JARs
17: CP="$GHIDRA_DIR/Ghidra/Framework/Utility/lib/Utility.jar"
18: if [ -d "$MCP_LIB" ]; then
19:     for jar in "$MCP_LIB"/*.jar; do
20:         CP="$CP:$jar"
21:     done
22: fi

24: # Get JDK path from LaunchSupport
25: LS_JAVA_HOME=$("$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -jdk_home -save 2>/dev/null || echo "$JAVA_HOME")
26: 
27: # Get VM args from LaunchSupport (handle \r\n line endings)
28: VMARGS=()
29: while IFS=$'\r' read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
30:     [ -n "$line" ] && VMARGS+=("$line")
31: done < <("$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -vmargs 2>/dev/null)

33: echo "[GhidraMCP] Starting Ghidra 12.1.2 with GhidraMCP embedded..."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GhidraMCP Launcher - Starts Ghidra with GhidraMCP classes in classpath
# GhidraMCP JARs are loaded via system classpath so ClassSearcher can find them.
# The extension must ALSO be in Extensions/GhidraMCP/ for runtime module resolution.
# Usage: ghidramcp [project_name]

set -e

export JAVA_HOME="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/jdk-21.0.11+10"
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"

GHIDRA_DIR="/mnt/dados/opencode/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC"
MCP_LIB_DIR="$GHIDRA_DIR/ghidramcp/lib"
SUPPORT="$GHIDRA_DIR/support"

# Build classpath: Utility.jar + all GhidraMCP dependency JARs
CP="$GHIDRA_DIR/Ghidra/Framework/Utility/lib/Utility.jar"
if [ -d "$MCP_LIB_DIR" ]; then
    for jar in "$MCP_LIB_DIR"/*.jar; do
        CP="$CP:$jar"
    done
fi

# Get JDK path from LaunchSupport
LS_JAVA_HOME=$("$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -jdk_home -save 2>/dev/null || echo "$JAVA_HOME")

# Get VM args from LaunchSupport (handle \r\n line endings)
VMARGS=()
while IFS=$'\r' read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    [ -n "$line" ] && VMARGS+=("$line")
done < <("$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -cp "$SUPPORT/LaunchSupport.jar" LaunchSupport "$GHIDRA_DIR" -vmargs 2>/dev/null)

echo "[GhidraMCP] Starting Ghidra 12.1.2 with GhidraMCP embedded..."
echo "[GhidraMCP] MCP server: http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp"
echo "[GhidraMCP] GhidraMCP JARs loaded from module classpath"
echo "[GhidraMCP] $((${#VMARGS[@]})) VM arguments loaded from LaunchSupport"
echo ""

cd "$GHIDRA_DIR"

# Tools state was cleared to remove stale FrontEndTool.xml references
# ClassSearcher will discover GhidraMcpPlugin + MCP server starts on plugin init()
exec "$LS_JAVA_HOME/bin/java" \
    "${VMARGS[@]}" \
    -showversion \
    -cp "$CP" \
    ghidra.Ghidra ghidra.GhidraRun "$@"
